desc:
Two tables are given as 2-D arrays. Each row is a pair [id, value]. Inside one table the ids are strictly increasing, so no id repeats within a table.

Merge the tables into one table that contains every id that occurs in at least one of them, sorted by id ascending. The value of an id is the sum of its values from the tables that contain it (a table that lacks the id contributes nothing).

For example, a = [[1,4],[3,2],[7,5]] and b = [[3,6],[4,1]] give [[1,4],[3,8],[4,1],[7,5]].
constraints: Each row has exactly 2 numbers: 1 ≤ id ≤ 1,000,000 and 1 ≤ value ≤ 1,000,000
Ids are strictly increasing inside a and inside b
hints: Because both tables are already sorted by id you do not need a full sort.
Walk through both tables with one index each, like the merge step of merge sort.
Compare the ids under the two indices. The smaller id is copied out; if they are equal, output the id once with the summed value and advance both indices.
editorial: Use two pointers i and j. If a[i].id < b[j].id, append a[i] and advance i; if it is larger, append b[j] and advance j; if the ids are equal, append [id, a[i].value + b[j].value] and advance both. When one table is exhausted, append the remainder of the other.
Time is O(n + m) because every row is looked at once. The alternative of putting everything into a dictionary and sorting the keys is O(n log n) and ignores the sortedness that the statement offers.
